title: Set your mind (Colossians 3:1–4)
hook: set your affection on things above
tomorrow: if you don't feel love, is putting it on just a costume?

segments.voice: Yesterday, roots out of sight and a wall going up, with thanks running over. Yesterday's line: rooted and built up.
screen: `ROOTED AND BUILT UP.` → `A RIDDLE IN CHAPTER THREE.`

segments.voice: A wedding ring goes on in about a second. Being married takes the rest of your life. Hold on to that, because Colossians three has a riddle in it. To living, breathing readers it says: "For ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God." Two verses later, a to-do list: "Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth." Mortify means put to death. So people who are already dead are told to put things to death? It reads like a glitch. It isn't.
screen: `A RING IN A SECOND, A MARRIAGE FOR LIFE.` → `YE ARE DEAD.` → `THEN, A TO-DO LIST?`

segments.voice: The chapter opens with an if: "If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God." Just before, Paul has said they were buried with Christ in baptism and raised with him. That's the ring: something that already happened to them. Then the line: "Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth." The title says set your mind; the King James says affection. Either way, it's where your attention keeps going back to. So here's the riddle solved. Dead, in Paul's sense, is a done deal: the old life buried, the real one hid with Christ, kept safe and out of sight. The to-do list is living as if that's true. And look at what's on the list. Not cloud-gazing. A few lines on: lie not one to another, put off anger, forgive. Things above don't pull anyone out of the kitchen. They change how people talk in it. One line from that list to tell a friend tonight. In this new life, Paul writes, "there is neither Greek nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, Barbarian, Scythian, bond nor free: but Christ is all, and in all." The labels people sort each other by don't come along. Then a promise: "When Christ, who is our life, shall appear, then shall ye also appear with him in glory." Hidden now. Shown later.
screen: `IF YE THEN BE RISEN.` · `SET YOUR AFFECTION ON THINGS ABOVE.` · `DEAD: A DONE DEAL. LIVING IT: DAILY.` · `HIDDEN NOW, SHOWN LATER.` · then, large: `THINGS ABOVE.`

segments.voice: Lift your eyes to the highest thing you can see from where you are: a corner of the ceiling, a treetop, a patch of sky. Each time your mind drifts to a replay or a worry, notice it, and set it back on that high point, the way you'd set a cup back where it belongs.
Set your mind. Paul's call in Colossians three: aim the attention on things above, and bring it home into ordinary life.
Your line: things above. Not away from the kitchen, but carried into it. Until tomorrow.

original.note: Greek: set your mind, think on, in Colossians 3:2. The King James renders it set your affection.

trapdoor: what you thought: set your mind on things above means daydreaming about heaven.
what it means: the old life is buried and the real one is hid with Christ; living as if that's true shows up in how you speak and forgive.
what a scholar hears: 'ye are dead' and 'mortify' sit two verses apart on purpose: a status already given, and a daily putting-off that follows.
guess: aim your attention on things above, on purpose
empty your head of every thought for a while
make a decision once and never change it again
recall: held from below, so able to grow

chat.meaning: Paul says set your affection on things above: aim the attention on purpose, and carry it into ordinary life, not away from it.

mortify.meaning: an old English word for put to death

affection.meaning: here, where the heart and attention are set

Scythian.meaning: a people from lands north of the Black Sea

baptism.meaning: the washing with water that marks a new life in Christ

notes: Puzzle shape: 'ye are dead' (3:3) beside 'Mortify therefore' (3:5). The wedding-ring picture is the writer's illustration (a status given at once, lived out daily), not from the text; confirm a Keeper is comfortable with it.
The baptism link is paraphrased from Colossians 2:12 ('Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with him'); churches understand baptism differently, so it is kept to what Paul says.
'lie not one to another' (3:9) is spoken unquoted as a paraphrase-in-passing; the list (3:8–13) is cited as paraphrase.
The earlier draft's claim about the Greek verb being 'a thinking word' and what 'newer versions' say was cut from the voice under the claims rule; the Greek stays in games.original. Confirm φρονεῖτε.
